method: Read the canonical HTML volume render list; inspected full section outlines and every named body-figure caption/anchor for all 16 numbered chapters; read targeted prose around suspected gaps, lifetime/ownership mechanisms, and shortlisted animation candidates; checked nearby figures, tables, margin art and selected cross-volume caption matches. This is a source/context planning audit, not an exhaustive sentence-level reading, rendered-art fidelity approval, or student study. No manuscript or artwork was edited. Frontmatter, part dividers, appendices, and the glossary are outside this numbered-chapter needs pass. Homepage/index sources were checked for scope but are not counted as numbered chapter rows.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: An orientation chapter: historical evidence, the D·A·M framework, the iron law, and lifecycle organization.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. Existing timeline, AlexNet, triad, growth plots, and lifecycle figure support this introductory level. Tables and equations already expose the iron-law terms; avoid an introductory dashboard that preempts later mechanisms.

keep_static.reason: An intersection landscape is fully spatial; sequential highlighting would merely repeat the prose.
Historical observations and dates do not become a causal experiment when animated.

chapters.title: System Paradigms
chapters.summary: Deployment tiers are compared through physical constraints and workload fit.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. Tier maps, decision screening, hybrid architecture, resource scorecard, and comparison tables already cover the argument. Hybrid arrows alone do not justify an animation.

keep_static.reason: A deployment spectrum supports side-by-side comparison without state change.
Static screening gates are useful to scan; highlighting one branch is not an animation mechanism.

chapters.title: ML Lifecycle
chapters.summary: Lifecycle ownership, contract gates, and investigation-driven feedback.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. The stage-interface table at lines 895–904 specifies artifacts and invariants; three existing lifecycle views cover loops and dependencies. A fourth lifecycle diagram would duplicate rather than clarify.

keep_static.reason: The feedback loop is a process map, already readable in one frame.
Survey responses are fixed evidence, not a time allocation simulation.

chapters.title: Data Engineering
chapters.summary: Data acquisition, validation, transformations, release, and accelerator feeding.
chapters.static_assessment: Coverage is broad, but training-serving consistency depends on persisted fitted state that is not shown in an existing body figure. Add one focused paired-path visual rather than another pipeline overview.

needs.title: One transformation, one fitted state, two execution paths
needs.evidence: The prose states that identical code still diverges when training and serving independently recompute normalization statistics. Lines 3297–3301 require training-only fitting and serialization with the model.
needs.existing_coverage: The chapter has generic pipeline and ETL/ELT maps plus audio representations, but none show fit versus apply or the state artifact. Chapter 14 discusses shared features without a paired fitted-state figure.
needs.proposal: A static paired-path diagram: training split fits mean/vocabulary once; frozen state and transformation version join the model release; validation/test/serving apply that state. Beside it, a same-raw-record parity inset shows the failure caused by independently fitted serving state.
needs.why_static: Print readers must distinguish executable code from learned preprocessing state and see the leakage boundary without playing anything.
needs.animation_value: Optional later interaction can switch shared versus independently fitted state and compare the same raw record. No moving pipeline boxes merely to repeat the definition.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

keep_static.reason: A framework taxonomy should stay glanceable.
Readers need to inspect the paired labels at their own pace; motion adds no information.

chapters.title: Neural Computation
chapters.summary: Neural arithmetic is mapped to batched machine work and memory lifetimes.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. The existing neuron-to-machine, training-step memory, byte-tier, loss, and roofline figures cover the difficult relationships unusually well. Animate selected lifetimes/reuse rather than adding another neural-network sketch.

animation_candidates.title: From Neuron to Machine
animation_candidates.reason: A row/column dot product becoming batched work makes weight reuse across examples visible.
sequence: Establish one input row and one weight column.
Form one output while retaining the weight tile.
Bring the next input row through the same retained tile.
Hold the output tile and compare distinct weight fetches with MACs.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Batching amortizes parameter movement; more arithmetic per fetch can raise intensity.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Optional batch-size selector, explicit toy tensor shapes and fetch accounting; no automatic speedup estimate.

animation_candidates.title: Memory Over One Training Step
animation_candidates.reason: Saved activations appear and disappear at specific consumer events; a final memory plot alone cannot show why each lifetime exists.
sequence: Forward creates each layer activation while weights/Adam buffers remain resident.
Backward consumes the final saved activation and creates gradients.
Release each activation only after its final consumer.
Optimizer updates, then preserve parameter state for the next step.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Training memory comprises distinct persistent and transient objects; a saved-activation peak need not equal total peak.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Batch selector linked to source accounting; separate inference adjacent-buffer reuse. Keep source numerical definitions.

keep_static.reason: A static size comparison already makes tier crossings clear; no need for a player around each bar.

chapters.title: Network Architectures
chapters.summary: Architecture families are explained by their access geometry, reuse, and resource constraints.
chapters.static_assessment: Convolution and prefill/decode already have appropriate body figures. A local depthwise/pointwise comparison is the main missing spatial relationship; the CNN overview and im2col figure do not show it.

needs.title: Standard versus depthwise-plus-pointwise convolution
needs.evidence: The section decomposes spatial filtering per channel and 1×1 channel mixing, then derives K²CinCout versus K²Cin+CinCout MACs.
needs.existing_coverage: fig-cnn shows one receptive field; fig-im2col-diagram shows lowering. Neither depicts separate channel filtering then mixing. No named depthwise/pointwise body caption was identified in the cross-volume caption search.
needs.proposal: Two matched small channel stacks: standard kernels spanning all input channels versus one spatial kernel per channel followed by a 1×1 mixer. Label the same input/output shapes, parameter/MAC expressions, and intermediate activation. Use a tiny declared schematic case rather than a new hardware benchmark. Label the MAC expressions per output spatial position; include N × Hout × Wout only when showing total work.
needs.why_static: The spatial/channel factorization must be understandable in print, including that it changes the model family and is not generally an algebraically identical replacement for an arbitrary trained dense convolution.
needs.animation_value: Animate separate per-channel filtering then channel mixing; an expanded knob can change Cin/Cout and display arithmetic plus intermediate bytes, without equating FLOP reduction with latency speedup.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

animation_candidates.title: Convolution Operation
animation_candidates.reason: The spatial relationship between one receptive field and its written output must be seen changing across positions.
sequence: Pin one shared kernel and select the first input patch.
Accumulate its contributions into one output cell.
Slide by the declared stride; retain kernel identity.
Write the next output and stop at the edge to explain valid-output dimensions.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Spatial weight sharing and overlapping input reuse differ from parameter count and arithmetic count.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Stride/padding/kernel selector with output-shape and MAC accounting; declare cross-correlation convention. Memory extension only where established.

animation_candidates.title: im2col Transformation
animation_candidates.reason: Overlapping input elements are duplicated into different lowered rows; motion can expose the expansion causally.
sequence: Identify one patch in both input channels.
Copy its elements into one lowered row.
Select the overlapping next patch and show repeated source elements copied again.
Multiply the lowered matrix by the stacked kernels and reshape the four output positions.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: GEMM-friendly layout can cost temporary storage and movement; the product and output indexing remain unchanged.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Toggle explicit materialization versus conceptual lowering; count exact toy expansion without claiming all convolution kernels materialize im2col.

animation_candidates.title: Prefill and Decode
animation_candidates.reason: This is the clearest existing anchor for prompt-wide work followed by sequential token generation and persistent cache state.
sequence: Process prompt positions together with causal visibility.
Write prompt K/V entries and produce the first generated token.
Feed that token into the next pass; read retained prior K/V and compute only new K/V.
Append the new entries, produce the next token, and hold the enlarged cache.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Caching removes recomputation of prior K/V while cache reads and bytes grow; small-batch weight reuse differs from prefill.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Prompt length, generated length, and batch selectors; separate per-layer cache toy geometry from whole-model accounting. Playback time is illustrative.

keep_static.reason: Published heterogeneous model reports cannot support arbitrary causal knob experiments.
Keep the architectural map for orientation; animate specific mechanisms in fig-prefill-decode instead.

chapters.title: ML Frameworks
chapters.summary: Framework graph execution, automatic differentiation, tensors, devices, and memory ownership.
chapters.static_assessment: Graph, dispatch, and tensor-layout coverage is strong. Reserved versus live allocator memory and fragmentation are described without a corresponding spatial snapshot; that distinction merits a small static figure.

needs.title: Live, cached, and fragmented allocator blocks
needs.section: #### Tensor lifetimes and the caching allocator {#sec-ml-frameworks-memory-management-gradient-computation-bb77}
needs.evidence: The caching-allocator section distinguishes saved-tensor lifetime, reserved pools, reusable blocks, and an allocation that fails despite aggregate free space (2635).
needs.existing_coverage: fig-training-step-memory in Chapter 5 plots live memory but does not show allocator-reserved memory or contiguity. Existing Chapter 7 graph figures name lifetimes without showing blocks.
needs.proposal: Three same-size pool snapshots: live tensors occupy blocks; released tensors leave allocator-cached blocks; a large contiguous request fails despite enough aggregate free capacity. Separate live, reserved, reusable, and total device usage in a compact legend. Declare a fixed/exhausted pool with no additional segment growth, compaction, or remapping. The request needs a contiguous virtual-address region, not physically contiguous DRAM.
needs.why_static: A static spatial counterexample is enough to explain why summing free bytes is insufficient and nvidia-smi does not diagnose allocator state.
needs.animation_value: Allocation/free/reuse is a promising later interaction, but use declared allocator policy and block sizes; do not imply all allocators have identical splitting or coalescing behavior. Keep virtual address space distinct from physical memory; fragmentation alone is not a universal OOM prediction.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

animation_candidates.title: Python Dispatch Overhead
animation_candidates.reason: Host dispatch, device queueing, idle gaps, and fused intermediate traffic are temporal dependencies.
sequence: Issue one host call and show queued device work.
Hold the idle gap before the next launch.
Replay the same operation chain under one fused submission.
Compare dispatch counts and intermediate write/read boundaries.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Fusion can reduce launch overhead and HBM intermediates, but does not guarantee proportional end-to-end speedup.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Explicit declared dispatch/kernel durations and fusibility assumptions, with equal arithmetic and no claimed universal timing.

animation_candidates.title: Tensor Memory Layout
animation_candidates.reason: Tracing logical neighbors into two physical orders makes stride arithmetic concrete without repeating a verbal definition.
sequence: Select a logical tensor cell.
Follow its row/column coordinate to an element offset in each order.
Advance one logical row or column and reveal actual neighboring storage cells.
Apply declared element byte width to distinguish element offset from byte offset.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Traversal locality depends on layout; strides count elements and precision converts offsets to bytes.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Traversal and byte-width choices; do not mutate storage silently or imply a view/transpose always copies data.

keep_static.reason: This stack categorizes responsibilities rather than changing state.

chapters.title: Model Training
chapters.summary: A training run is assembled from compute, data supply, optimizer state, and memory-saving methods.
chapters.static_assessment: Prefetch and checkpointing are already illustrated. FlashAttention has a long mechanism discussion, pseudocode, roofline arrow, and margin ladder but no body-level dataflow illustration in Volume I. Reuse/adapt the existing Volume II artwork before commissioning new art.

animation_candidates.title: Illustrative Overlapped Data Prefetching
animation_candidates.reason: The benefit is independent batches progressing on different resources with buffers and dependencies, not simply shorter bars.
sequence: Run one batch through open/read/train.
While the GPU trains it, fill the next batch’s separate buffer.
At completion swap ready buffers and continue.
Hold remaining idle regions and compare equal stage durations with the sequential baseline.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Overlap hides some producer latency while preserving finite resource capacity and data readiness.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Declared stage durations and prefetch depth with bounded buffers; paired fig-fetching-naive supplies baseline.

animation_candidates.title: Gradient Accumulation
animation_candidates.reason: Gradient accumulation and parameter updates occur at different boundaries.
sequence: Compute micro-batch one and retain its gradient contribution.
Free its activations after backward; keep parameter values fixed.
Add contributions from remaining micro-batches with explicit loss normalization.
Apply exactly one optimizer update and reset the accumulation buffer.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Effective update batch can grow without holding all activations simultaneously; gradients/state still occupy memory.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Equal and unequal micro-batch sizes to reveal weighted normalization; disclose stochastic/batch-dependent layer caveats.

animation_candidates.title: Activation Checkpointing
animation_candidates.reason: The saved/recomputed/consumed lifetime is difficult to infer from static storage marks.
sequence: Forward keeps selected checkpoints and releases unsaved intermediates.
Backward reaches a segment whose internal activation is missing.
Recompute the segment from its retained checkpoint.
Consume reconstructed values and free them only after final backward use.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Checkpointing exchanges recomputation for saved activation storage, with transient reconstructed memory still required.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Checkpoint placement and batch size; compare stored/live totals under a declared schedule rather than quoting universal square-root savings.

keep_static.reason: Diagnostic choices should remain inspectable without a playback sequence.

reuse_opportunities.title: Attention intermediates: HBM materialization versus SRAM tiling
reuse_opportunities.evidence: Lines 4781–4795 describe streaming tiles, running maximum/normalizer, rescaling partial output, and never writing full score/probability matrices to HBM.
reuse_opportunities.existing_coverage: Local fig-training-roofline shows the consequence, not the mechanism; a margin ladder compares only sizes. The mechanism already exists in books/vol2/09_performance_engineering/09_performance_engineering.qmd:2002, fig-performance-engineering-flashattention-tiling.
reuse_opportunities.proposal: Reuse or simplify the Volume II figure into a paired conventional/tiled attention view for Volume I: persistent Q/K/V/O in HBM, current tile and running m/l/output in SRAM, explicit score/probability writeback present only in the baseline. Cross-reference the later detailed treatment.
reuse_opportunities.why_static: Print readers need to see which tensors disappear from HBM and which remain; the pseudocode and roofline arrow alone do not establish storage boundaries.
reuse_opportunities.animation_value: Strong later candidate: stream two KV tiles, show a larger second-tile max rescale the earlier contribution, commit normalized output, compare equal results and declared HBM materializations. Never present asymptotic FLOP reduction or tile size as total peak memory.
reuse_opportunities.asset_strategy: reuse or simplify existing Volume II figure; local introductory coverage, not a new book-wide concept
reuse_opportunities.reason: Print readers need to see which tensors disappear from HBM and which remain; the pseudocode and roofline arrow alone do not establish storage boundaries.

chapters.title: Data Selection
chapters.summary: Selection is evaluated as an end-to-end cost decision, including the physical data path.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. Existing selection inequality, acquisition loop, boundary selection, and ResNet data-path figure cover the major relationships. Avoid animating illustrative accuracy curves as if they were executable predictive models.

animation_candidates.title: ResNet-50 Data Path on One H100
animation_candidates.reason: The same selection fraction may remove arithmetic without removing upstream decode/read traffic.
sequence: Trace one full-epoch baseline through storage, CPU, PCIe, GPU.
Materialize a coreset and show which earlier bytes disappear.
Apply stream-and-discard selection and retain the upstream bytes it still reads/decodes.
Add one scoring pass or stored teacher targets and account for their separate cost.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: A smaller training set is not automatically a faster data pipeline; placement determines which resource is relieved.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Selection fraction/materialization/scoring choices with source-derived per-epoch budgets and explicitly separate one-time versus recurring cost.

keep_static.reason: Selection criteria are a static decision aid.
Synthetic conceptual curves are not a learned predictive model to manipulate.

chapters.title: Model Compression
chapters.summary: Structural compression, numerical representation, and supported execution are separated.
chapters.static_assessment: No addition identified. Quantization has extensive static coverage from distributions through affine mapping and integer pipeline. The priority is clear transformations and costs in selected existing figures, not more compression diagrams.

animation_candidates.title: Quantized Matrix Multiplication Pipeline
animation_candidates.reason: Represented values, stored codes, retained wide sums, and output requantization are different objects that should visibly transform.
sequence: Show real input and nearest representable level.
Store indexed INT8 codes with explicit scales and zero-points.
Read one operand pair, subtract zero-points, and add its product to the retained INT32 sum.
After the reduction, requantize and apply the declared activation in the source pipeline order.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Lower-width operands reduce representation bytes; wide accumulation and output conversion preserve different numerical roles.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Scale/range/precision controls reveal rounding and clipping; align exact order with caption/art before implementation. Arithmetic detail remains optional.

animation_candidates.title: Calibration Range Selection
animation_candidates.reason: Changing an affine mapping reveals the precision-versus-clipping tradeoff that a static pair only samples.
sequence: Establish a fixed observed distribution and fixed code budget.
Fit a symmetric range and mark unused codes for a skewed distribution.
Switch to asymmetric mapping with a zero-point and the same code budget.
Narrow or widen the range and hold clipped samples and level spacing.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Choosing range allocates finite codes and changes both rounding error and saturation; asymmetric mapping is not guaranteed best quality.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Range and outlier toggle with a fixed declared distribution; compare reconstruction error without equating it with model accuracy.

animation_candidates.title: Block Sparse Representation
animation_candidates.reason: Metadata determines which dense subblocks are read and computed; empty space alone conveys no executable saving.
sequence: Establish equal dense input and output semantics.
Read the index array to locate one nonzero block.
Gather its matching operand block and update a retained output tile.
Skip a declared empty block and show value bytes plus metadata bytes.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Regular sparse storage can avoid work only through matching kernels; representation/index overhead matters.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Block occupancy and block size under a toy supported format; no measured latency or universal break-even claim.

keep_static.reason: Compression tiers are a static organizing frame.
Workflow choices and validation burden should not receive decorative tours.

chapters.title: Hardware Acceleration
chapters.summary: Accelerator compute, memory tiers, bounds, and mapping explain attainable execution.
chapters.static_assessment: Tiling, systolic flow, sparse selection, host transfers, and accelerator anatomy already exist. The missing complementary mechanism is how identical logical payload can produce different transactions and exposed latency under irregular addressing.

needs.title: Useful payload, transferred cache lines, and dependent addresses
needs.evidence: The prose distinguishes scattered accesses wasting cache-line payload, pointer/index dependencies limiting parallelism, and route imbalance.
needs.existing_coverage: The regular/irregular comparison table at 2769–2780 names the regimes; accelerator anatomy and tiling show hierarchy/reuse but not transaction geometry. DLRM pipeline in Chapter 6 shows row gathers without physical cache-line cost.
needs.proposal: Two paired small address strips: adjacent lane requests share fetched lines, scattered requests use more lines for the same payload; add a separate dependent index→payload timeline so bandwidth waste and exposed latency cannot be conflated. State illustrative line/lane sizes. Declare the illustrative transaction/sector/cache-line granularity and cold-cache/no-reuse conditions before counting fetched bytes; logical addresses alone do not establish physical DRAM traffic.
needs.why_static: Static address grouping and the dependency arrow make two different bottlenecks visible before introducing any time-based controls.
needs.animation_value: Issue the same logical reads in adjacent/scattered modes, count useful/transferred bytes, then separately reveal serial dependent versus concurrent requests. No measured transaction latency unless source-backed.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

animation_candidates.title: Systolic Array Dataflow Architecture
animation_candidates.reason: Operand arrival alignment and retained partial sums define the actual matrix product.
sequence: Establish a small declared dataflow and stationary object.
Inject skewed rows/columns so matching reduction indices meet.
Advance one conceptual cycle and update each PE’s partial sum.
Drain final outputs and hold fill/drain idle slots.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Local forwarding/reuse reduces repeated external reads, while array utilization depends on mapping and matrix dimensions.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Small shape and stationary-policy choices only after each policy has a technically verified schedule; illustrative cycles are not product benchmarks.

animation_candidates.title: 2:4 Structured Sparsity GEMM
animation_candidates.reason: Compact indices select the correct matching dense operand positions; skipping zero glyphs is not enough.
sequence: Partition each supported sparse group into four positions.
Retain exactly two nonzero values and their position metadata.
Use metadata to select the matching dense elements.
Accumulate an output and compare identical dense/sparse arithmetic results.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Supported structured sparsity changes the inner-loop representation and work; metadata and nonaccelerated work limit total gain.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Declared 2:4 pattern selector; reject invalid groups and distinguish pruning quality loss from executing already-pruned values.

animation_candidates.title: Matrix Tiling Mechanics
animation_candidates.reason: Tiles move between storage tiers while partial sums must remain live across every reduction tile.
sequence: Load one A/B tile pair into fast storage.
Compute and retain the partial C tile.
Replace operand tiles for the next reduction slice and add to the same C.
Write C only after the full reduction; compare reuse with a declared naive schedule.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Tiling trades finite fast-memory capacity for fewer off-chip reads; residency and dependencies constrain tile choice.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Tile dimensions and SRAM budget; exact toy byte accounting, with no proportional runtime promise.

keep_static.reason: The architecture remains useful as a static reference; detailed data movement belongs in the selected mechanisms.
Dated trend data should remain visibly fixed and qualified.

chapters.title: Benchmarking
chapters.summary: Benchmarking fixes workload, measurement boundaries, and the evidence required for comparisons.
chapters.static_assessment: Existing taxonomy and power-boundary figures are useful. Two invisible timing mechanisms in the harness section remain prose-only: host enqueue versus completed work, and coordinated omission under a stall. These are stronger additions than more benchmark-suite maps.

needs.title: What an asynchronous benchmark timer actually measures
needs.evidence: A host-level call enqueues accelerator commands and returns before device work completes; explicit synchronization or device events bound the intended work.
needs.existing_coverage: fig-granularity describes scope; Chapter 7 dispatch timelines describe starvation, not measurement start/stop boundaries. No local body figure distinguishes host enqueue timing from device elapsed time.
needs.proposal: Aligned host and device lanes with enqueue, device queue, kernel, and completion events. Overlay a short naive host timer and correctly labeled synchronization/device-event intervals; explicitly distinguish kernel-only from transfer-inclusive/end-to-end boundaries.
needs.why_static: The interval endpoints and included work are the argument and should be inspectable on a printed page.
needs.animation_value: A later single-step reveal can move timer endpoints or toggle warm/cold state and show omitted work. Keep elapsed figures illustrative and avoid implying all synchronization timers isolate kernel time.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

needs.title: Coordinated omission during the same server stall
needs.evidence: The section compares independent arrivals during a 500 ms stall with a closed-loop client that sends no additional queries while blocked.
needs.existing_coverage: Existing latency/throughput curves in Chapter 13 show queue effects, while Chapter 12 benchmark maps and tables do not show arrival suppression.
needs.proposal: Two aligned timelines replay one declared stall: open-loop arrivals continue and queue; one-request closed-loop client waits and suppresses attempted arrivals. Mark what each harness records, and distinguish the two offered workloads.
needs.why_static: Print readers must see that the client changes arrivals, rather than merely plotting a misleading summary percentile.
needs.animation_value: Animate arrivals, backlog, completions, and recorded latencies under the two harnesses; do not claim a single closed-loop request means every real workload should be open loop.
needs.asset_strategy: new local artwork only after confirming proposed relation is absent from existing assets

keep_static.reason: A workflow checklist does not require motion merely to enumerate stages.
Measurement boundaries should remain explicit and inspectable without a player.

chapters.title: Model Serving
chapters.summary: Serving joins request latency, batching, persistent cache state, and throughput budgets.
chapters.static_assessment: Existing prefill/decode coverage belongs in Chapter 6 and the KV-budget plot is already here. The strongest local gaps concern token-level admission scheduling and logical-to-physical KV blocks; adapt later-volume diagrams or add explicit pointers before commissioning new art. Speculative verification is already illustrated in Volume II performance engineering (fig-speculative-decoding, line 3463), so start with a cross-reference rather than add a third local illustration.

animation_candidates.title: Request Pipelining
animation_candidates.reason: Independent request identities and readiness make resource overlap understandable.
sequence: Track request A through CPU, transfer, GPU, and output.
Prepare request B while A occupies the accelerator.
Dispatch B only when input and resource dependencies permit.
Hold throughput improvement alongside each individual request’s latency.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Pipelining improves duty cycle and throughput without necessarily reducing per-request service latency.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Source stage durations and bounded queued requests; separate batching and network delay from the figure’s declared boundary.

animation_candidates.title: The KV-Cache Explosion
animation_candidates.reason: A growth plot earns interaction only when connected to actual per-request cache allocation and release.
sequence: Reserve model weights and explicitly leave runtime overhead outside or budget it.
Prefill requests and attribute bytes to their prompt positions.
Decode one token per active request and add the corresponding per-layer K/V bytes.
Complete a request and release its owned cache, updating the plotted operating point.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Weights are relatively fixed while request state scales with batch and total retained context; capacity limits concurrency.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Context/batch/GQA/precision controls tied to declared model shape and consistent decimal/binary units. Pair with new paging diagram rather than claiming paging shrinks bytes/token.

keep_static.reason: A compatibility map is not a simulation of format support.
Historical price points should not appear to predict live economics.

reuse_opportunities.title: Token-level continuous batching and chunked-prefill admission
reuse_opportunities.evidence: The section explains that long prefill can stall active decode and that admitting bounded chunks limits interference.
reuse_opportunities.existing_coverage: fig-serving-pipeline-timing covers CPU/I/O/model overlap, not autoregressive scheduling. fig-prefill-decode in Chapter 6 covers one request. A later detailed timeline already exists at books/vol3/05_kv_cache/05_kv_cache.qmd:889, fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.
reuse_opportunities.proposal: Adapt the Volume III timeline to an introductory shared-request schedule: request identities persist, short requests finish and free slots, a waiting request joins; compare one whole prefill admission against chunked admission beside active decodes. Keep total work and timing assumptions explicit.
reuse_opportunities.why_static: The request boundary versus token-iteration boundary and effect on inter-token gaps should remain visible in the printed comparison.
reuse_opportunities.animation_value: Strong animation after figure approval: each Next advances one scheduling decision or token boundary; show prefill chunks and decode output markers with distinct cues. Optional lab changes prompt/generation lengths and admission limits, not arbitrary animation speed as latency.
reuse_opportunities.asset_strategy: adapt existing later-volume figure for local introductory coverage; prefer cross-reference if adequate, no new concept art
reuse_opportunities.reason: The request boundary versus token-iteration boundary and effect on inter-token gaps should remain visible in the printed comparison.

reuse_opportunities.title: Logical KV pages, physical blocks, and release
reuse_opportunities.evidence: PagedAttention maps per-sequence logical pages to noncontiguous physical blocks and returns completed sequences’ blocks to a free pool.
reuse_opportunities.existing_coverage: The local margin art shows wasted space only, and fig-kv-cache-growth shows aggregate capacity only. Reuse/adapt books/vol2/10_inference/10_inference.qmd:3505, fig-paged-attention, which already presents an eight-slot example.
reuse_opportunities.proposal: A concise introductory logical-page→block-table→physical-pool snapshot, paired with contiguous allocation of the same cache contents. Include a partially occupied tail block and ownership legend. Cross-reference the detailed later-volume treatment rather than invent a second incompatible example.
reuse_opportunities.why_static: Addresses, ownership, and free capacity are indispensable static relationships; print cannot rely on following a moving block.
reuse_opportunities.animation_value: Strong later animation: allocate prompt blocks, read through mapping, append without moving prior blocks, finish request, release only owned blocks, admit another. Paging does not shrink KV bytes per token or guarantee a throughput multiplier.
reuse_opportunities.asset_strategy: adapt existing later-volume figure for local introductory coverage; prefer cross-reference if adequate, no new concept art
reuse_opportunities.reason: Addresses, ownership, and free capacity are indispensable static relationships; print cannot rely on following a moving block.

chapters.title: ML Operations
chapters.summary: Operational release, retraining, drift, and incident response share finite node resources.
chapters.static_assessment: The node-day occupancy timeline already makes release-control memory and contention concrete. A missing paired version/state depiction would clarify why reverting weights alone may not restore a stateful ranker.

needs.title: Rollback includes the embedding namespace
needs.evidence: The ranker example explains that version 2 can rotate or resize embeddings, making cached vectors meaningless to version 1; rollback must switch compatible state along with weights.
needs.existing_coverage: tbl-rollback-patterns lists state handling; fig-ml-ops-dlrm-node-day covers resource residency and canary capacity, not embedding compatibility. fig-ops-cicd covers artifacts at pipeline level.
needs.proposal: Two versioned bundles, each containing weights, feature schema, and embedding/cache namespace. Compare a mismatched rollback (old weights with new vectors) with an atomic routing/namespace switch; quarantine training logs from the degraded interval separately. Pin model/schema/embedding versions per request during coexistence; the routing switch must not silently migrate in-flight requests or repair historical logs.
needs.why_static: Readers need to see compatibility links rather than infer that a rollback arrow repairs all accumulated state.
needs.animation_value: Only animate if the reader can observe actual request routing and compatible state ownership across a switch; a static version-pair diagram may be sufficient. No generic CI/CD box-highlighting tour.

animation_candidates.title: One Ranking Node's Day
animation_candidates.reason: Model copies and a retraining job compete for the same finite accelerator slots over time.
sequence: Keep serving and immediate-rollback copies resident.
Start retraining in remaining slots.
Complete retraining and retain the candidate artifact separately.
Load the canary into freed slots, then show when earlier copies can safely retire.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Rollback immediacy consumes real residency, and release schedules can be capacity constrained even if serving alone fits.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Compare hot versus reload-based rollback under the chapter’s declared copy sizes and schedule; distinguish artifact-on-disk from loaded resident copy.

Measured historical cohort comparisons remain evidence plots.

chapters.title: Responsible Engineering
chapters.summary: Responsibility is expressed through evidence gates, subgroup outcomes, governance, and feedback.
chapters.static_assessment: Threshold, frontier, lifecycle, and governance figures cover static choices. Selective outcome observation after deployment is a separate causal mechanism currently carried by prose and a worked recurrence; add one evidence-flow diagram.

needs.title: Decisions select the outcomes the next model observes
needs.evidence: Denied credit applicants produce no routine repayment labels; the previous policy selects the retraining population. Independent audit evidence is needed to observe outcomes outside that selection.
needs.existing_coverage: fig-responsible-lifecycle is a governance process, fig-fairness-threshold is a static outcome choice, and Chapter 14 drift plots show external changes. None show censored labels and policy-driven sampling.
needs.proposal: Credit-service loop with applicants, approve/deny gate, observed repayment only for approved applicants, and retraining from observed labels; mark missing outcomes explicitly. A separate, declared approval-sampling intervention followed by actual outcome observation supplies additional valid evidence. Do not imply an audit can reveal counterfactual repayment for a denied loan. Keep the first figure focused on the censored-label path; omit the optional disparity trace.
needs.why_static: The missing-data path must be visible in print so readers cannot mistake absence of labels for negative labels or assume all-population TPR is directly observable.
needs.animation_value: Strong later animation can replay two declared rounds with persistent applicant groups and observed/unobserved outcomes; a toggle adds the stated audit/approval-sampling intervention. Do not animate the fitted exponential recurrence as a universal fairness law or guarantee an ethical intervention.

animation_candidates.title: Threshold Effects on Subgroup Outcomes
animation_candidates.reason: A threshold movement changes specific decisions and subgroup error counts on the same fixed observations.
sequence: Establish the fixed labeled markers and subgroup identities.
Move from the first stated boundary to the second.
Identify exactly which decisions changed.
Update subgroup confusion counts and hold the aggregate accuracy versus subgroup error tradeoff.
animation_candidates.systems_takeaway: Aggregate improvement can conceal a worsening subgroup outcome; evaluation needs per-slice evidence.
animation_candidates.expanded_lab: Threshold inspection on this declared constructed dataset only; avoid claiming a universal fairness-accuracy frontier or inferring causality from a smooth animation.
